## Body

PR #280 round 2 at c8d2eab2fc9e073d8c8b8de27dbb53e8141ec315: Busy must remain UNKNOWN through destructive decisions, and must not consume retry bookkeeping. The observer returns before retirement; unknown reaper evidence cannot tombstone; locked revive needs explicit Some(false); kill propagates inventory error before launch; postlaunch observation errors preserve the dispatched seat and pane. The Codex binder nevertheless saves Seen at codex_bind.rs:253-256 before probing, so a transient error can suppress a later attempt. This is F232, explicitly assigned as a non-blocking C34 follow-up for #280, with a separate fix to avoid marking failed probes seen. An independent correctness-review diagnostic with another process holding the lock measured 30 Busy reads in 4.039625 ms, zero forks, and a primed 50 ms timer at 53.234916 ms; release enabled exactly one control launch. Zero launches applies only to the initial five-second grace. Persistent holding later enters fork fallback and five-second startup backoff; that backoff is not a per-read fork throttle. Difficulties: availability changes require tracing both mutation guards and retry markers; a fast read-only review gate remains unavailable in dependency-free checkouts. Magic wand: a focused held-lock consumer fixture that proves no false retirement and no consumed retry trigger, without adding a new final-round gate.
